messages.content: Explain what a write-ahead log is, then check the docs.

content.text: A write-ahead log records every change before it is applied to the main data files. When the database crashes, it replays the log from the last checkpoint, so no committed transaction is lost and no half-applied change survives. Writers append to the end of the log, which is sequential and fast, while the data pages are updated later in the background. Readers can keep using the old pages until the checkpoint moves them forward. The log also makes replication simple, because a replica only needs to apply the same records in the same order.

attempts.content: A write-ahead log records every change before it is applied to the main data files. When the database crashes, it replays the log from the last checkpoint, so no committed transaction is lost and no half-applied change survives. Writers append to the end of the log, which is sequential and fast, while the data pages are updated later in the background. Readers can keep using the old pages until the checkpoint moves them forward. The log also makes replication simple, because a replica only needs to apply the same records in the same order.

Checkpoints bound recovery time by flushing dirty pages and recording how far the log has been applied. Without them the log would grow forever and every restart would replay it from the very beginning. Most engines checkpoint on a timer or once the log passes a size threshold, and they do it incrementally so writers are not stalled. After a checkpoint, the log segments before it can be recycled or archived for point-in-time recovery, which is how backups can be restored to an exact moment rather than only to the time of the last full copy.
